title: PAC Learning Intuition
interviewAnswer: PAC learning formalizes whether enough samples let a learner find, with high probability, a hypothesis whose true error is approximately small.
why: PAC provides a clean vocabulary for learnability and sample complexity.
intuition: The question is how much data is needed so a learned model is likely to be good enough, not whether it can be perfect.
deepDive: Bounds connect hypothesis complexity, desired error ε, confidence δ and sample size. Classical bounds can be loose but reveal qualitative dependencies.
commonMistakes: Treating PAC bounds as exact data calculators.
production: Use theory for intuition and empirical validation for actual deployment decisions.
workedExample: A simpler class may need fewer samples to control generalization but can have more approximation bias.
